Topping the charts in 47 countries, including the United States, the United Kingdom, Canada, Australia, Germany, France, Italy and Spain, and reaching the top 10 of six others, "Despacito" has been listed among the best Latin songs ever by various publications, with some referring to it as one of the most successful Spanish-language tracks in pop music history.[[3]](#cite_note-3) It has been credited by music journalists as being the most instrumental song in spreading the popularity of Spanish-language music in the mainstream global market since "[La Bamba](/wiki/La_Bamba_(song)#Los_Lobos_version "La Bamba (song)")" by [Los Lobos](/wiki/Los_Lobos "Los Lobos") in 1987 and "[Macarena](/wiki/Macarena "Macarena")" by [Los Del Rio](/wiki/Los_del_R%C3%ADo "Los del Río") featuring the Backside Boys in 1995.[[4]](#cite_note-:0-4)[[5]](#cite_note-:1-5)

In the United States, it became the first Spanish-language song to top the [*Billboard* Hot 100](/wiki/Billboard_Hot_100 "Billboard Hot 100") since "Macarena" in 1996, subsequently tying as the [longest-reigning number one on the *Billboard* Hot 100](/wiki/List_of_Billboard_Hot_100_chart_achievements_and_milestones#Most_weeks_at_number_one "List of Billboard Hot 100 chart achievements and milestones") at the time with 16 weeks, as well as becoming the [longest-running number one on the Hot Latin Songs chart](/wiki/List_of_Billboard_Hot_Latin_Songs_chart_achievements_and_milestones#Most_weeks_at_number_one "List of Billboard Hot Latin Songs chart achievements and milestones") with 56 weeks from 2017 to 2026.[[6]](#cite_note-:3-6) It became the second Spanish-language song to be nominated for the [Grammy Awards](/wiki/60th_Annual_Grammy_Awards "60th Annual Grammy Awards"), earning nominations for [Song of the Year](/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Song_of_the_Year "Grammy Award for Song of the Year"), [Record of the Year](/wiki/Grammy_Award_for_Record_of_the_Year "Grammy Award for Record of the Year"),

Main article: [List of countries and territories where Portuguese is an official language](/wiki/List_of_countries_and_territories_where_Portuguese_is_an_official_language "List of countries and territories where Portuguese is an official language")

The [Community of Portuguese Language Countries](/wiki/Community_of_Portuguese_Language_Countries "Community of Portuguese Language Countries")[[55]](#cite_note-CPLP-55)
(in Portuguese *Comunidade dos Países de Língua Portuguesa*, with the Portuguese acronym CPLP) consists of the nine independent countries that have Portuguese as an [official language](/wiki/Official_language "Official language"): [Angola](/wiki/Angola "Angola"), [Brazil](/wiki/Brazil "Brazil"), [Cape Verde](/wiki/Cape_Verde "Cape Verde"), [East Timor](/wiki/East_Timor "East Timor"), [Equatorial Guinea](/wiki/Equatorial_Guinea "Equatorial Guinea"), [Guinea-Bissau](/wiki/Guinea-Bissau "Guinea-Bissau"), [Mozambique](/wiki/Mozambique "Mozambique"), [Portugal](/wiki/Portugal "Portugal") and [São Tomé and Príncipe](/wiki/S%C3%A3o_Tom%C3%A9_and_Pr%C3%ADncipe "São Tomé and Príncipe").[[55]](#cite_note-CPLP-55)

[Equatorial Guinea](/wiki/Equatorial_Guinea "Equatorial Guinea") made a formal application for full membership to the CPLP in June 2010, a status given only to states with Portuguese as an official language.[[56]](#cite_note-56) Portuguese became its third official language (besides [Spanish](/wiki/Spanish_language "Spanish language") and [French](/wiki/French_language "French language"))[[57]](#cite_note-57) in 2011, and in July 2014, the country was accepted as a member of the CPLP.[[58]](#cite_note-58)

Portuguese is also one of the official languages of the Special Administrative Region of the People's Republic of China of Macau (alongside [Chinese](/wiki/Chinese_language "Chinese language")) and of several international organizations, including [Mercosul](/wiki/Mercosul

**Paul Anthony Pierce** (born October 13, 1977) is an American former professional [basketball](/wiki/Basketball "Basketball") player. He played 19 seasons in the [National Basketball Association](/wiki/National_Basketball_Association "National Basketball Association") (NBA), predominantly with the [Boston Celtics](/wiki/Boston_Celtics "Boston Celtics").

Pierce was a high school [McDonald's All-American](/wiki/McDonald%27s_All-American "McDonald's All-American") before earning consensus first-team [All-America](/wiki/NCAA_Men%27s_Basketball_All-Americans "NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans") honors as a [junior](/wiki/Junior_(education_year) "Junior (education year)") playing [college basketball](/wiki/College_basketball "College basketball") for the [Kansas Jayhawks](/wiki/Kansas_Jayhawks_men%27s_basketball "Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball"). After being chosen by the Boston Celtics with the 10th overall pick in the [1998 NBA draft](/wiki/1998_NBA_draft "1998 NBA draft"), Pierce spent the first 15 years of his career with Boston. Pierce's nickname, "**the Truth**," was given to him by [Shaquille O'Neal](/wiki/Shaquille_O%27Neal "Shaquille O'Neal") in 2001. He earned 10 [All-Star](/wiki/NBA_All-Star_Game "NBA All-Star Game") selections and became a four-time [All-NBA](/wiki/All-NBA "All-NBA") team member throughout his 19 year career. Pierce combined with [Kevin Garnett](/wiki/Kevin_Garnett "Kevin Garnett") and [Ray Allen](/wiki/Ray_Allen "Ray Allen") in 2007 to form a "Big Three" that led Boston to two [NBA Finals](/wiki/NBA_Finals "NBA Finals") and an [NBA championship in 2008](/wiki/2008_NBA_Finals "2008 NBA Finals"). Pierce was named [NBA Finals Most Valuable Player](/wiki/Bill_Russell_NBA_Finals_Most_Valuable_Player_Award "Bill Russell NBA Finals Most Valuable Player Award") in 2008. Walmart :: Operating divisions :: Sam's Club :: chunk_0032
Main article: [Sam's Club](/wiki/Sam%27s_Club "Sam's Club")

**Sam's Club** is a chain of [warehouse clubs](/wiki/Warehouse_club "Warehouse club") that sell groceries and [general merchandise](/wiki/General_merchandise "General merchandise"), often in bulk.[[32]](#cite_note-Volpe-36) Locations generally range in size from 32,000–168,000 sq ft (3,000–15,600 m2), with an average club size of approximately 134,000 sq ft (12,400 m2).[[151]](#cite_note-2022_10-K-155) The first Sam's Club was opened by Walmart, Inc. in 1983 in [Midwest City, Oklahoma](/wiki/Midwest_City,_Oklahoma "Midwest City, Oklahoma")[[291]](#cite_note-aboutsamsclub-295) under the name "Sam's Wholesale Club". The chain was named after its founder Sam Walton. As of October 31, 2022, Sam's Club operated 600 membership warehouse clubs and accounted for 11.3% of Walmart's revenue at $57.839 billion in fiscal year 2019.[[292]](#cite_note-xbrlus_1-296)[[293]](#cite_note-297) Christopher Nicholas is the president and CEO of Sam's Club.[[150]](#cite_note-leadership-154)[[294]](#cite_note-298)

Based in San Bruno, California, Walmart's Global eCommerce division provides online retailing for Walmart, Sam's Club, and all other international brands. There are several U.S. locations in California and Oregon: [San Bruno](/wiki/San_Bruno,_California "San Bruno, California"), [Sunnyvale](/wiki/Sunnyvale,_California "Sunnyvale, California"), [Brisbane](/wiki/Brisbane,_California "Brisbane, California"), and [Portland](/wiki/Portland,_Oregon "Portland, Oregon"). Locations outside of the United States include [Shanghai](/wiki/Shanghai "Shanghai") (China), [Leeds](/wiki/Leeds "Leeds") (United Kingdom), and [Bangalore](/wiki/Bangalore "Bangalore") (India).

The most restricted meaning of *continent* is that of a continuous[[13]](#cite_note-13) area of land or mainland, with the coastline and any land boundaries forming the edge of the continent. In this sense, the term *[continental Europe](/wiki/Continental_Europe "Continental Europe")* (sometimes referred to in Britain as "the Continent") is used to refer to mainland Europe, excluding islands such as [Great Britain](/wiki/Great_Britain "Great Britain"), [Iceland](/wiki/Iceland "Iceland"), [Ireland](/wiki/Ireland "Ireland"), and [Malta](/wiki/Malta "Malta"), while the term *continent of Australia* may refer to the [mainland of Australia](/wiki/Mainland_Australia "Mainland Australia"), excluding [New Guinea](/wiki/New_Guinea "New Guinea"), [Tasmania](/wiki/Tasmania "Tasmania"), and other nearby islands. Similarly, the *[continental United States](/wiki/Contiguous_United_States#Continental_and_mainland_United_States "Contiguous United States")* refers to "the 49 States (including [Alaska](/wiki/Alaska "Alaska") but excluding [Hawaii](/wiki/Hawaii "Hawaii")) located on the continent of North America, and the [District of Columbia](/wiki/Washington,_D.C. "Washington, D.C.")."[[14]](#cite_note-14)

From the perspective of geology or [physical geography](/wiki/Physical_geography "Physical geography"), *continent* may be extended beyond the confines of continuous dry land to include the shallow, submerged adjacent area (the [continental shelf](/wiki/Continental_shelf "Continental shelf"))[[15]](#cite_note-15) and the islands on the shelf ([continental islands](/wiki/Island#Continental_islands "Island")), as they are structurally part of the continent.[[16]](#cite_note-16)

United States Infantry Colors as depicted in National Geographic, 1917

The flag's official proportions are 33:26, which is notably shorter than many other state flags. However, in practice, the flag is often produced and sold in 5:3 ratios.[[3]](#cite_note-3)[[4]](#cite_note-4)

[![](//upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/5/5b/Greater_coat_of_arms_of_the_United_States.svg/250px-Greater_coat_of_arms_of_the_United_States.svg.png)](/wiki/File:Greater_coat_of_arms_of_the_United_States.svg)

The greater coat of arms of the United States of America.

According to state law, the design of the flag mirrors that of the First North Dakota Infantry's standard during the [Spanish–American War](/wiki/Spanish%E2%80%93American_War "Spanish–American War") and the [Philippine–American War](/wiki/Philippine%E2%80%93American_War "Philippine–American War").[[5]](#cite_note-hist-5) This makes the flag similar to [the greater coat of arms of the United States](/wiki/Great_Seal_of_the_United_States "Great Seal of the United States"), and nearly identical to many other regimental standards, [and current state flags](/wiki/Seal_on_a_bedsheet "Seal on a bedsheet").

A banner with the national coat of arms was carried by all infantry regiments from 1890 to 1904, with the sole distinction being the unit designation inscribed on the scroll underneath the coat of arms.[[6]](#cite_note-ReferenceA-6) The regimental colors of the North Dakotan troops, for instance, were adorned with the inscription "1st North Dakota Infantry".
